title: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL)
also: kidney stone removal through the back
what: The surgeon makes a small opening in your back right into the kidney, breaks up the stones, and takes them out. The surgery is done under general anesthesia.
why: For large kidney stones, when other methods are not suitable.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours; the hospital stay is usually a few days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Allergies, including to medicines and iodine
Heart, lung, or kidney disease, or diabetes
If you or your relatives had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a checkup with a general doctor. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Scans
prepare.text: A CT scan of the kidneys is usually needed so the surgeon can see the stones.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, the anesthesiologist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before and no drinks for a few hours before. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

bring: Your CT scans on a disc
Things for a few days in the hospital
steps: On the day of surgery, you change, and an IV line is placed in your vein
In the operating room, you get anesthesia and fall asleep
Using X-ray or ultrasound, the surgeon makes an opening into the kidney through your back
Through it, the stones are broken up and removed
Often a tube is left from the kidney to the outside, plus a catheter in the bladder
You wake up in the recovery room
feel: After anesthesia, you may feel sleepy and sometimes sick
Pain in your side and back. You will get pain medicine
Some blood in the urine for the first few days is common
after: The tubes are usually removed after a few days. The doctor will tell you
Drink more water, unless your doctor told you to limit fluids
No heavy lifting or sports for a few weeks
A stone analysis can help prevent new ones. Talk with your doctor
red_flags: A fever over 38°C with chills: call emergency services
Severe pain in your side or belly
A lot of blood or clots in the urine
Urine leaking from the opening after you go home

faq.q: Why not break up the stones from outside, without an opening?
faq.a: Large, hard stones do not break up well from outside. The surgeon chooses the method based on the size and place of the stone.
They can. Your doctor will advise on diet, drinking, and tests to lower the risk.

reminders.text: Kidney surgery tomorrow. Bring documents, CT scans, and your list of medicines. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
